subject: design/executor-lifecycle-delivery
statement: The executor report package provides distinct implementation-completed, task-delivered, and plan-completed events plus an opt-in durable Reporter. Registered handlers receive stable event identities in persisted publication order; failed handlers block their own later transitions while successful independent handlers retain their receipts. One reporter exclusively owns each ledger through an OS lock until Close or process exit.
intent: Make consequential lifecycle reactions recoverable across storage failures and process restarts without losing events, overwriting another run, or repeating durably completed siblings.
rationale: Publish records an event before any sink or handler sees it. Unsaved admissions and outcomes are flushed before further effects. Handlers remain idempotent across the unavoidable effect-to-receipt crash window. Ordinary progress does not drain pending work; Publish returns errors, Emit reports failures through an observer or structured log, and Resume retries pending work explicitly. Lifecycle owners still supply verified transitions and handlers; this change adds the reporting substrate rather than wiring production completion predicates.
fit_criterion: Package regressions cover admission and receipt save failures, malformed state, cancellation, immutable payload identity, cross-process exclusive ownership, crash recovery after a real subprocess exits between effect and receipt, ordered retries across restart, all presentation sinks, and concurrent duplicate publication under the race detector.
